newsitem.title: GERMANY: German public broadcasters stabilise in ad income.
newsitem.headline: German public broadcasters stabilise in ad income.

text.p: German television channels saw modest gains in advertising income in 1986 but public broadcasters' ad sales idled, the German central advertising association (ZAW) said on Tuesday.
The German television industry as a whole posted a relatively weak 8.7 percent rate of growth in 1996 to 6.9 billion marks after several boom years.
But the two national public broadcasting networks, which are only permitted to carry advertisements before 8 p.m., saw a 0.8 point drop in ad market share to 9.4 percent.
The ZAW said this fall was due to "steady expansion by private stations in the ad market".
Television ranks second behind newspapers among mass media in Germany for advertising income. The ZAW said 1996 was the first year in a decade that TV posted only single-digit gains in ad sales.
The association said the industry's slight boost in ad income during 1996 was partly due to heavier investment in television advertising by medication and detergent manufacturers and beer brewers.
The ZAW monitors the posted financial data of the German advertising industry and results annually.
